cases.outcome: Login restores the original route. `UseNhAuthentication` builds the authentication endpoints once, so routing and the application-wide endpoints share them. cases.title: Microsoft OAuth
cases.outcome: The management app starts a Microsoft sign-in and the callback completes it only in that browser: the OAuth state is a protected, ten-minute flow with a PKCE verifier and nonce, bound by a correlation cookie for the configured callback path behind the app's /api proxy, and used once. A callback from another browser or with a state the application did not issue, changed or let expire answers 400 without a session, and the sign-in returns only to a path of the application or one of the sample's allowed origins. The sign-in finds its local account by the ID token's tenant and object id: the first sign-in of an account in the developer's directory, named in `AllowedTenantIds`, links the local account whose user name is its mail once, and an account of another directory with the same mail signs in to nothing.

cases.title: Refresh token
cases.outcome: A refresh token rotates at most once while independent device sessions remain usable, and the platform authentication services pass startup validation. cases.title: Session expiration
cases.outcome: The live countdown expires, token state is cleared, and both apps open login with a reason and return URL. cases.title: Logout

A custom logout route configured through `LogoutEndpoint` is mapped to the logout endpoint.

cases.title: Impersonation
cases.outcome: A visible impersonation banner is displayed. The impersonation session has no refresh token, so it ends with its access token and can never turn into an ordinary session of the impersonated user, and a custom `ImpersonateEndpoint` route is independent of the refresh route. The token carries a digest of the security stamp of the user who started the impersonation (`NhPlatformClaimTypes.ImpersonateOriginSecurityStamp`), so the session validator ends it once that user changes the password and while that user is locked out or blocked.

cases.title: Revert impersonation

cases.title: Durable background operation with fan-out and nested progress
cases.surface: `WithBackgroundOperations`, `INhBackgroundOperationHandler<T>`, `TaskResult`, `INhBackgroundOperationNotificationPolicy`, `NhBackgroundOperationRetryResult`, fan-out/fan-in, durable leases, scoped polling, scoped SignalR at `NhBackgroundOperationsOptions.HubPath`, and cross-owner administration through `UseAdministrationPolicy`, `INhBackgroundOperationAdministrationService`, `INhBackgroundOperationOwnerDirectory`, and `NhBackgroundOperationAdministrationService`
cases.outcome: A division-exclusive parent durably fans out project work, releases its worker while children execute concurrently, propagates expected batch, checkpoint, step, and fan-in outcomes through TaskResult, reschedules internal lock contention without consuming handler retries while a heartbeat skips a beat instead of contending with its own attempt's write, advances a contended final-child wake-up to the next dispatcher interval, serializes reconciliation, dispatch claims and cancelled completions with operation writers so event sequences remain unique, aggregates nested progress, notifies the owner only about outcomes and requests for attention while threading repeated portfolio work per division through a notification policy, protects unprojected notification milestones during event retention, starts under strict EF Core warning policies, and remains isolated to the authenticated user and accessible active division through notifications, SignalR, and polling. An opt-in administration policy lets administrators list every owner's root operations in the accessible active division plus global operations with the owner's display name, inspect operator-only events and scheduling diagnostics, and cancel or retry on the owner's behalf; the administrator is recorded as the cancellation requester so the owner is notified, the endpoints return 404 until a policy is configured, host start fails when the configured policy is not registered,, the owner-facing API never exposes operator-only events, and the list stays usable for very large tables through status filters, capped pages, summary projections without payloads, polling that pauses while hidden, and an index that skips fan-out children. Dispatchers only claim operations on the Hangfire queues their own process serves, and an operation that no worker starts fails with dispatch-stalled after MaxDispatchRecoveries reconciliation rounds instead of cycling forever, with an operator-only diagnosis of the queue, the Hangfire job state and whether a worker serves the queue. The `nh-background-operations` readiness check is degraded only by work that is stuck, by the reconciler's definitions: an attempt whose heartbeat is stale, or work that has been due for `StaleAttemptTimeout` on the application's clock and unchanged for as long on the system clock, so debounced and backed-off work, signal waits and a jump of the application's clock keep an application ready. A cancellation whose worker stopped, an attempt being cancelled whose heartbeat went stale, is finished by reconciliation as the worker would have finished it: cancelled once with the cancellation milestone, the stale attempt's leases released and its late writes refused on fencing, and a fan-out parent cancelled once its children ended; the readiness check counts it until then. A running attempt whose heartbeat went stale spends a retry as a failed attempt does, so an operation whose handler never returns fails with stale-attempt-retries-exhausted once its retries are spent instead of being retried without end. Controllers and the hub ask the platform's `INhActorContextAccessor` and `INhDivisionAccess` who the user is and which division they may use, which NewHeap Identity answers from the request and its division claims. The sample keeps the hub at its default path `/hub/background-operations` and documents `HubPath` next to the operation URL prefix: any absolute application path below the root outside the operations' API under `/background-operations` is accepted, NewHeap's bearer setup reads the query token at that path, and a host with the hub at `/realtime/operations` connects a WebSocket there with the token in the query string and receives its owner's operation changes. cases.title: S3 media storage
cases.outcome: Configuration validates bucket, region, and credentials without logging secrets.

cases.title: Media authorization
cases.outcome: Read, mutate, and delete operations respect the active user and division: the media routes admit only signed-in users, the path must lie in the active division's projects, and the user's current application permission or user-store division permission authorizes it; no request header grants a permission. Every mutation is authorized where it writes: a move or rename is also authorized as a create at its destination and refuses a name the destination already holds, and tag updates and localizations are authorized as updates of the file, so a division manager cannot place or retag media in another division and a viewer cannot localize. The media endpoints answer a refusal with 401 and an existing name with 409.

cases.title: Folder lifecycle

cases.title: File upload and download

The stored name chooses the content type from the library's fixed list, `application/octet-stream` for any other name; raster images are served inline, every other file as an attachment, always with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so an uploaded page is saved instead of rendered.

cases.title: Media search and sorting

cases.title: Thumbnails

cases.title: Read-only database diagnostics
cases.surface: `newheap-db` direct schema and JSON query contracts plus consumer-owned governed schema, indexes and query MCP tools
cases.outcome: Developers and agents take the repository-declared database fast path without inspecting application code, settings, secrets or package internals to rediscover routing or JSON fields: one bounded tracked-file search finds a nested catalog, its directory becomes the diagnostic working directory, and its only profile automatically selects the provider, configuration path, connection-string name, ceilings and default environment. Local `validate` opens no connection and advertises the `outbound-network` capability required by `schema` and `query`; Codex starts those execution commands with a narrow reusable `newheap-db` network permission instead of first probing its restricted sandbox. When the user explicitly requests another runtime environment, `--environment` applies it consistently to schema and query without requiring a duplicate profile solely for Production or Staging; the governed connection-string name and read-only-principal verification remain unchanged. `newheap-db` resolves that name through the selected environment's normal configuration and secrets flow without exposing the connection string. A direct `schema --search ... --describe-if-single` invocation needs no JSON schema request and returns a unique match plus its exact columns, indexes and relationships through one connection and read-only transaction; zero or multiple matches remain bounded summaries. `schema` and `query` validate internally, so interactive diagnostics do not spend a separate call on `validate`. The executable sample prompt uses Production from a Development-default profile, counts projects and returns the latest by `CreationDateTime` with exactly one schema invocation and one query invocation. Checked-in schema and query requests remain repeatable CI and dry-run contracts. Permission-filtered exact descriptions expose named outgoing and incoming relationships with ordered column pairs and validation status, while at most one focused index lookup may inform an immediately useful predicate or ordering. Structured MCP input and the direct CLI `--request-file` option keep serialized JSON out of Windows process arguments. The executable sample MCP fixes profile, capability, a sixteen-call budget and ceilings server-side, requires an explicit requested row count, rejects excessive requests before execution, and fails without partial data when actual results exceed the accepted limit, while SQL Server and PostgreSQL enforce dedicated read-only credentials and return only safe provider classifications, codes, stages and retry hints. Principal rejection on SQL Server and PostgreSQL also returns an optional first rejected verificationCheck such as function-select or predefined-role-membership; PostgreSQL verification denies by default across the principal and every role it can use, so a predefined role other than pg_read_all_data, an administrative pg_catalog function, a function in a pg-prefixed user schema, a column or view write and sequence usage are rejected while a SELECT-only principal passes; SQL Server verification also rejects VIEW SERVER STATE, ALTER ANY CONNECTION, impersonation, ALTER ANY SCHEMA, sequence UPDATE, schema and object ALTER or TAKE OWNERSHIP and column UPDATE by name and then denies every other permission beyond connecting, SELECT and metadata visibility, while db_datareader still passes. The PostgreSQL query policy refuses its forbidden functions also as quoted, schema-qualified or case-varied identifiers and functions that run SQL text such as query_to_xml, and refuses Unicode-escaped identifiers and escape strings before a connection opens, while standard_conforming_strings stays on in the diagnostic transaction. The guidance keeps the platform's credential-bearing tables (refresh tokens, AspNetUserTokens, NotificationDeliveries) and the AspNetUsers password-hash and security-stamp columns outside the SELECT allowlist and replaces database-wide read grants with per-table grants on such a database. The MCP preserves allowlisted checks without exposing principal or object names, tolerates older responses without the field, and leaves the permission policy unchanged. Unknown connection failures become transient `connection-failed` outcomes without weakening `authentication-failed` or `database-not-found`, and no server name, credential or provider exception text reaches the response. An unresolved NewHeap secret returns `connection-string-unresolved` with the process-local secrets-path remediation, while malformed resolved provider configuration returns `connection-configuration-invalid`; neither exposes its value or produces schema or query evidence. A checked-in exact local path may be applied to the `newheap-db` child process for one schema retry without permanently changing Production settings. Every other non-success governed schema response ends the diagnostic attempt, so agents do not infer deployed identifiers, relationships, enum values or business semantics from source code or a repository index and do not issue a data query. A server certificate the host does not trust returns the non-transient `tls-certificate-untrusted` with the `certificate-authority-trust-required` retry hint instead of a transient `connection-failed`, proved through real TLS handshakes on both providers, and the sample MCP maps it to a trust remedy without the provider message. A schema search may omit the schema, the search term or both on SQL Server and PostgreSQL.

cases.title: Generated local read-only AI tool
cases.outcome: A compile-time generated local function searches only the active division supplied by the authorized invocation context; typed schema binding, bounded input and mandatory budget reservation run before application work, while a denied, oversized or incomplete invocation never reaches the read service. Optional explicit MCP/AIDAP export names are unique, version-independent manifest contracts, while tools without the attribute retain their existing generated wire names. The model receives the shared `NhAiToolResult` shape: `{ success, data }` for a search, and for a context without an active division `{ success: false, code: "project-division-scope-missing", message }`, so it can tell that failure apart from every other one and explain it; the generated function publishes that shape as its return schema. Every `[Authorize]` policy on the method, the tool set or their base declarations, named or positional, reaches the descriptor the tool gate enforces, and roles, authentication schemes or `AuthorizeAttribute` subclasses fail the build with `NHAI018`.

cases.title: Named AI model profile
cases.surface: `AddNewHeapPlatformAI`, `AddChatProfile`, keyed `IChatClient`, startup validation, Development container validation, and `INhAiModelProfileResolver`
cases.outcome: A consumer-owned deterministic chat client resolves through a stable project-assistant profile only when its declared capabilities, classification, execution region, budget, keyed client and fail-closed budget manager satisfy startup validation. A worker that shares the AI composition without an invocation gate passes Development scope and build validation and fails clearly only when it resolves the tool invoker.

cases.title: Authorized AI tool discovery
cases.surface: `INhAiToolDiscoveryService`, default-deny `INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy`, generated catalog exposure, and scoped capability grants

cases.title: Generated tool over MCP
cases.surface: `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`, `INhAiMcpToolAdapter`, `CallNewHeapToolAsync<TInput, TOutput>`, official ASP.NET Streamable HTTP and in-memory MCP transports, generated `AIFunction`, the shared discovery/invocation pipeline, and the message format of a failed result: `NhAiMcpResultMetadata.MessageFormatKey` and `MessageArgumentsKey` with their bounds, and `NhAiMcpToolException.FailureMessageFormat` and `FailureMessageArguments`
cases.outcome: The API publishes the same generated project search implementation through the official stateless ASP.NET MCP transport. Every list and call resolves the current authenticated request independently; actor- and tenant-specific discovery, invocation authorization, budget, cancellation, input bounds and structured `TaskResult` errors remain in the shared NewHeap pipeline. A typed .NET client passes generated input directly through the official helper, which creates the `input` envelope, honors explicit JSON options including omitted optional null properties, returns the typed `TaskResult<T>.data` value, and preserves failed MCP tool results in `NhAiMcpToolException`. A search query longer than 200 characters fails with `project-search-query-too-long` and a message declared as a `FormattableString`; the failed result keeps the text `code: message` and also carries the message's format and arguments in `_meta` (`newheap.com/message-format`, `newheap.com/message-arguments` with `[200,240]`), which the client exception exposes and the sample test renders with the client's own text for that format and its own culture, falling back to the server's text for a format it does not know. Only generated catalogs and attested runtime catalogs (see SPM-243) enter the NewHeap export path; a catalog without MCP exposure, such as a run-scoped imported catalog (see SPM-228), is skipped. Independently governed external SDK tools can coexist under distinct wire names and continue using the official SDK directly, while duplicate NewHeap publication and export-name collisions fail at startup.

cases.title: Authorized ASP.NET AI context
cases.surface: `INhAiAuthenticatedInvocationContextResolver`, `AddNewHeapPlatformAIAspNet`, `NhAiAspNetIssuerClaimMapping`, configurable single- and multi-issuer OIDC claim projection, `IAuthorizationService`, execution scopes, and narrow capability grants; recognizing the request's person by the actor id the registered `INhAiAuthenticatedInvocationContextResolver` resolves, not by a claim, in the context contributor, the agent gate's request turns (`NhAiAgentInvocationScope.IsRequestTurn` with `DelegateFromInitiator`) and consultations
cases.outcome: The production ASP.NET gate resolves a fresh context per request. Hosts with unmapped JWT claims accept one exact issuer through the source-compatible overload or multiple issuer mappings with issuer-specific claim types and scopes. Each principal resolves through exactly one authority mapping, the same subject under different issuers produces different actor IDs, and missing, duplicate, multi-authority or unaccepted issuer claims return typed failures. The existing active-division flow remains available and contributes scope only after server-side policy authorization; request cancellation propagates. In the initiator's own request an agent turn acts with the request's principal, recognized by the issuer-qualified actor id the resolver resolves rather than by a claim, while another person's turn in the same request gets nothing from it.

cases.title: Approved and verified AI mutation
cases.surface: `NhAiProposal`, `NhAiApproval`, `INhAiAuthoritativeExecutionEvidenceValidator`, `INhAiCapabilityResolver`, `INhAiBudgetManager`, `INhAiIdempotencyManager`, `INhAiToolVerifier`, `INhAiToolConcurrencyLimiter` with `UseInProcessConcurrencyLimiter` and `NhAiToolConcurrencyPartition`, `NhAiAuditRecord.ResultCode` and `IdempotencyCode` with `NhAiToolFailureCodes`, and the shared invocation pipeline
cases.outcome: An agent can change one project status only inside its authorized division and narrow manage capability after authoritative approval and mandatory budget reservation; the same idempotency key cannot repeat or alter the side effect, and success is reported only after an independent status read verifies the result. The audit names the code each caller received: none for the verified change, and `ai-tool-idempotency-denied` as the `ResultCode` of the refused retry, next to the lease's own `IdempotencyCode` `duplicate`; every other refusal of the invoker audits its own code the same way. Consumers may validate their existing authoritative approval and idempotency evidence into a bounded attestation without creating a second Platform proposal model, while all execution still passes through the shared invoker. Tool concurrency is bounded per tenant: while one tenant's search fills its `MaxConcurrency`, another tenant's search runs, and a further search from the first tenant is refused with `ai-tool-concurrency-limited` before it reaches the read service.

cases.title: Policy-bound Agent Framework adapter
cases.surface: `NhAiAgentDescriptor`, `INhAiAgentFrameworkAdapter`, `NhAiAgentCreateRequest.EffectsAsProposals` with `NhAiAgentInvocationScope.RequireApprovalForEffects`, Microsoft Agent Framework `ChatClientAgent`, named model profiles, and generated Agent-exposed tools, and `NhAiAgentCreateRequest.ChatHistoryProviderFactory` and `AIContextProvidersFactory` with Agent Framework `ChatHistoryProvider` and `AIContextProvider`, and `NhAiAgentModelCallException.Code`

An agent with Propose autonomy only reads, also with the rights to change projects, until the runtime turns every change into a proposal: in a scope that requires approval for effects, `EffectsAsProposals` offers it the status tool as well. The project agent keeps the messages of its session in the `InMemoryChatHistoryProvider` its request's `ChatHistoryProviderFactory` creates: the second question reaches the model with the first exchange, through the governed client and with only the published search tool. The library tests add an AI context provider whose instructions reach the model while a tool it adds fails the run before the model is called, and a failed governed call reaches the agent as `NhAiAgentModelCallException` with its failure code, such as `ai-model-timeout`.

cases.title: Governed external MCP tool import
cases.surface: `INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`, explicit per-server allow-list and namespace, local effect and authorization metadata, bounded remote schemas and results, run-scoped `INhAiToolCatalog` registration, and shared invocation governance, and opt-in per-call request metadata through a reviewed `INhAiMcpInvocationBinder` (`AddNewHeapPlatformAIMcpInvocationBinder`, `NhAiMcpImportedToolPolicy.InvocationBinderId`, `NhAiMcpRequestMetadata`, `NhAiMcpInvocationIdentity`), `NhAiMcpImportedToolPolicy.AllowAgentGrant` for organization credentials and `NhAiMcpCallContext` for credential decisions in the client transport
cases.outcome: Only the explicitly allowlisted external lookup is imported under a collision-safe namespace; its remote description grants no authority, an unlisted destructive-looking tool remains absent, and bounded arguments still cross NewHeap authorization, capability, budget, timeout, concurrency, idempotency, result-bound, and audit controls. A run-scoped catalog over the tools a run imported passes Development container validation, is validated in its own startup scope, serves the agent through the shared invoker and stays out of the NewHeap MCP export of the same host. A binder registered for one server and tool adds `_meta` only to a policy that names it, runs after authorization, capability, approval, budget and idempotency checks, counts toward the input limit, binds its id into the tool contract and stops the call with an audited code when it fails. The agent receives the shared `NhAiToolResult` shape with the remote `CallToolResult` as `data`; a remote `isError` result fails with `ai-mcp-remote-tool-error` and keeps the remote result as `data`, while verifiers still receive the typed `CallToolResult`. During the remote call, and only then, `NhAiMcpCallContext.Current` carries the authorized invocation context to the client transport; a policy that allows agent grants publishes an agent-grantable descriptor with its own contract hash.

cases.title: Durable external-signal suspension and wake-up

cases.outcome: A running operation atomically suspends its attempt and releases the worker, accepts one owner-bound typed signal, treats an identical duplicate idempotently, rejects a conflicting signal, resumes as a new fenced attempt, preserves completed idempotent work, and remains cancellable or expiry-wakeable without polling.

cases.title: Approval-gated durable AI portfolio report

cases.title: Authorized provider-neutral AI ingestion

cases.outcome: A division-scoped document is never opened before read and replacement-delete authorization, remains untrusted data with provenance and classification, and is embedded only after an immutable source/document/version lease plus mandatory model-budget reservation succeed; denial or conflict performs no embedding or vector write.

cases.title: Content-free AI model usage and streaming telemetry
cases.surface: `INhAiChatExecutor`, named profile and run-budget enforcement, OpenTelemetry activities and metrics, `INhAiUsageSink`, token/latency/TTFT accounting, and cancellation-safe streaming, and `NhAiUsageRecord.ModelCallId` with `NhAiBudgetRequest.ModelCallId`: one id per governed model call that its retries, budget reservation, `ai.model.invoke` activity (`newheap.ai.model_call_id`) and usage record share, and the failed result `NhAiModelFailureCodes.Timeout` with `NhAiOutcomeKind.TimedOut` and `NhAiModelFinishReasons.TimedOut` for a governed deadline

Each governed model call has its own `ModelCallId`, which its retries, its budget reservation and its usage record share, while `InvocationId` keeps naming the invocation context that several calls share. A governed deadline, the profile's timeout or the run's deadline, ends a call or a stream with the failed result `ai-model-timeout` and a usage record and activity with outcome `TimedOut` and finish reason `timed-out`, while the caller's own cancellation still throws; both reserve the budget once and write one usage record.

cases.title: Versioned AI safety evaluation gate
cases.surface: Microsoft `IEvaluator`, `NhAiEvaluationDataset`, deterministic scope and injection fixtures, fail-closed metric interpretation, content-free reports, and baseline version/hash evidence; the malicious-document case `document-instructions-remain-data` of the `project-document-safety` dataset, scored on a recorded assistant turn
cases.outcome: The project agent's prompt-injection and cross-division fixtures run through Microsoft AI Evaluation contracts against a versioned baseline; missing or inconclusive interpretations fail closed, while persisted reports contain hashes and metric outcomes but no prompt, response, reason or diagnostic content. A second dataset scores a recorded turn of the project assistant with a malicious Word document whose text tells the model to ignore its instructions and approve everything: the text reaches the model only through the example reader, behind the external-file marker as untrusted retrieved data and never in the instructions; the turn offers the same tools as without the document, the status change the model then asks for waits for the person's approval and nothing runs, and the business audit holds the file's id, normalized name, type, reader and SHA-256 but never its text, while the platform audit and the logs hold neither its text nor its name.

cases.title: Native AOT generated AI tool catalog smoke
cases.surface: `NewHeap.Platform.AI.AotSmoke`, generated `INhAiToolCatalog`, canonical schema manifest, trimming, and Native AOT publication
cases.outcome: A trimmed Native AOT executable resolves the generated catalog and creates its local Microsoft AI function without runtime reflection discovery, proving descriptors and schema manifests remain rooted.

cases.title: Durable AI ingestion lifecycle
cases.surface: `INhAiBackgroundOperationIngestionAdapter`, content-free checkpoints, deterministic replacement lineage, authorized deletion, and partial-success batch results

cases.title: Version-bound Agent Framework workflow checkpoint

cases.outcome: An official Agent Framework workflow checkpoint retains its opaque session and checkpoint identity in a content-free durable reference; a changed workflow version, checkpoint lineage or state hash cannot be resumed as the same run.

cases.title: SQLite exact and regex redirects and embedded MVC administration
cases.surface: NhProxyRedirectRule, NhProxyRedirectPathMatchMode.Regex, INhProxyConfigurationService, INhProxyAdministrationService, NhProxySqliteLoginAuditStore, NhProxyOptions.ConfigureYarp, AddNewHeapProxy, UseNewHeapProxy, MVC regex checkbox and local draft testing, MapProxyEndpoints, NhProxyApiResult, optional Basic management API, NhProxyChangeAuditEvent, INhProxyChangeAuditStore, ConfigureAdministrationAuthentication, ConfigureApiAuthentication, NhProxyAdministrationAuthenticationOptions, NhProxyApiAuthenticationOptions
cases.outcome: Hosting at the origin root with an empty PathBase is supported; hosting under a subdirectory is unsupported and deferred until a concrete use case requires it. A consumer starts the proxy with AddNewHeapProxy and UseNewHeapProxy, loads literal redirects from SQLite before requests, and manages rules in the embedded MVC panel with host-owned credentials. The administration sample binds UserName and Password from environment variables, the recommended live deployment setup. Consumers install NewHeap.Platform.AspNet.Proxy.Sqlite with its neutral proxy dependency; both belong to the independent nuget-proxy release unit. The sample uses local projects while release packaging retains the published Common dependency version. Password is hashed once at startup and cleared from proxy options; PasswordHash remains an alternative and configuring both fails startup. Neither credentials nor their hashes belong in committed settings. Password-based startup creates a fresh salted hash and requires a new administration login after restart. The configuration service commits and activates changes immediately with revision conflict protection. The panel tests unsaved literal rules locally and records login IP/outcome auditing. A sign-in from an address outside the IP allowlist is refused before the shared login budget, so it spends none of the administrator's attempts; the audit records such denied attempts up to LoginAttemptLimit per LoginAttemptWindow, and ProxyAdministrationSamplesTests signs the administrator in after twice that many denied attempts through the host's forwarded headers. Native YARP and host authentication remain independent; stored rewrite editing and managed-rule draft testing are demonstrated by SPM-239. The opt-in Development-only Proxy demo profile provides a fixed local test account and seeds one literal redirect in a separate SQLite file without resetting edits on restart. The Aspire AppHost starts this profile independently with an assigned port, an administration dashboard link and a health check. The regex checkbox opts into matching the escaped path plus query; captures build the entire destination without automatic query merging. Exact matching semantics remain unchanged, and regex rules survive SQLite restart. A root-relative target and every regex expansion are validated as the path the Location carries after dot segments, including %2e, are removed, so an expansion that resolves to a network path (//host) passes through instead of redirecting. NewHeapProxy:Limits:RedirectResolutionTimeoutMilliseconds configures the shared exact/regex resolver budget, defaulting to 50 ms and captured at startup; expiry or regex timeout returns HTTP 503 with no-store and no downstream execution. Each regex receives the remaining budget as its native engine timeout, so matching itself stops without abandoned background work. The persisted HTTP sample binds a 75 ms timeout and demonstrates the timeout response and a successful subsequent request. Registration tests retain the 50 ms default, and the draft tester follows the configured budget. The optional MapProxyEndpoints call before UseNewHeapProxy exposes a server-to-server Basic API under /newheap-proxy/api; without the call it stays unavailable. It reuses host administrator credentials and the IP allowlist without issuing cookies, creating login records or consuming browser login attempts. Bad API credentials have their own failure budget. HTTPS is required outside Development and Origin-bearing requests are denied. Before saving, the shared validator builds native YARP transforms and compiles regex route constraints, including disabled rules, without backend requests. Malformed route/transform patterns are rejected before changing configuration, revisions or audit. Invalid JSON, including missing transform kinds, returns 400 with a readable issue message and JSON field path; rejected requests do not save or audit. cases.title: Consumer-authoritative AI writes with issued grants and a flat MCP schema
cases.surface: `NhAiApprovalRequirement.ConsumerAuthoritative` and `Issuer`, `NhAiApprovalRole`, `NhAiIdempotencySupport.ConsumerAuthoritative`, `NhAiEffectDecisionKind.ConsumerAuthoritativeApproval`, `NhAiAuthoritativeExecutionEvidence.Denied`, `NhAiToolExportSchema.Flat` with `NhAiToolJsonSerializerOptions.FlatExport`, `NhAiToolHint` annotation overrides and `NhAiToolAnnotationHints`, serializer-contract-aware generated schemas, `NhAiToolFailureCodes` and `NhAiMcpResultMetadata`, `NhAiAuditRecord.ApprovalCode`, `ApprovalEvidenceReference`, `ResultCode` and `AnnotationOverrides`, `CallNewHeapFlatToolAsync<TInput, TOutput>` with `NhAiMcpToolException<TPayload>`, and the shared invocation pipeline
cases.outcome: An issuer tool creates a single-use project status grant under the application's own manage authorization; it declares the Issuer approval role, takes no Platform idempotency lease and is audited with the approval code `issuer`. The consuming write declares consumer-authoritative approval and idempotency. Its authoritative evidence validator burns every presented grant and returns an invalid, expired or replayed grant as the typed domain receipt with execution `deny`, database completion `not-executed`, the stable code `approval-invalid-expired-or-replayed` and a bounded evidence reference; the invoker copies that receipt into the failed `TaskResult<T>.Data` and audits the denial code and evidence reference. A replayed idempotency key passes the validator, reaches the engine and returns the reconciled receipt with `idempotentReplay: true` while the Platform idempotency manager is never asked for a lease. The flat MCP export publishes the input properties as top-level arguments and the receipt as the structured result, written compactly with every property including null `committedAt`, and a generated schema whose names, string enum values and optional properties match that serializer contract. The consuming write publishes `destructiveHint: true` through a narrowing hint override without changing its governance; widening overrides fail at generation and publication. Every failed call publishes its code, message and evidence reference in `_meta`; failures without data publish `{ code, message }` and the text `code: message`; the typed client throws `NhAiMcpToolException<ProjectAiStatusReceipt>` with `Code`, `FailureMessage`, `EvidenceReference` and the typed `Payload`. Tools that do not opt in keep Platform approval and leases, an effect policy cannot delegate approval to a tool that did not opt in, and destructive effects still require Platform approval and a verifier.

cases.title: Hangfire hosts in one process
cases.surface: `WithHangfire`, its `consoleOptionsAction`, Hangfire.Console, per-host `JobStorage`, `JobActivator` and `IBackgroundJobClient`, and process-wide Hangfire configuration
cases.outcome: Hosts composed with `WithHangfire` start one after another, after earlier hosts were stopped and disposed, and side by side in one process. Each host runs its jobs against its own storage with its own services and still attaches job console output, because Hangfire.Console is registered once per process and reused. A later host that requests different console options fails with a Platform error naming the conflicting option instead of the Hangfire.Console initialization exception. Single-host applications keep their existing behavior.

cases.title: API bridge catalog over MVC controllers
cases.outcome: The API publishes its project and project-task controller actions as the `sample-api` tool set without writing tool classes. Descriptors come from ApiExplorer: GET actions are read-only, PUT/PATCH are idempotent mutations and POST actions are mutations; every non-read tool requires approval and an idempotency key, while DELETE, anonymous, upload and policy-less actions are never published. A user discovers a tool only when the controller's own `[Authorize(Policy = ...)]` policies succeed for that user, so a viewer sees only reads and a project manager also sees create and update; the curated `projects.*` tools keep their existing discovery policy as the inner policy. Calls run through `INhAiToolInvoker` and then through the API's own HTTP pipeline as the signed-in user with only the caller's bearer token, `Accept-Language`, `Idempotency-Key` and the invocation id forwarded; a denied mutation stops before any HTTP call with `ai-tool-authorization-denied`, and HTTP failures reach the model as `{ success: false, code, message }` with stable `api-bridge-*` codes and without response text. Arguments sent without the `input` envelope run once with the same request, while `input` mixed with other properties returns `ai-tool-input-invalid` and never reaches the API. In an agent turn the bridge sends the request's token only inside the initiator's own request turn: a turn that runs in another person's request, such as an approver's decision that continues the initiator's turn, and a headless turn send nobody's token and fail with api-bridge-unauthenticated before any HTTP call.

cases.surface: `INhAiAttestedToolCatalog`, `NhAiToolCatalogAttestation.Validate`, `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`, `INhAiMcpToolAdapter`, `EnableMcpExposure` and the `<toolset>_<tool>_v<version>` export names of the API bridge
cases.outcome: Because the bridge catalog attests that every function is an `INhAiGovernedAIFunction` bound to its descriptor and runs through `INhAiToolInvoker`, it enters the same MCP export path as generated catalogs. The API's `/mcp` endpoint lists `sample-api_project_get_v1` and the other read tools for a viewer, adds create and update tools only for a project manager, and calls them through the same discovery, invocation gate, approval, idempotency, budget and result-bound pipeline. The attestation is validated at startup; a host whose bridge catalog is not attested cannot start.

cases.title: Attested catalog validation rejects ungoverned functions
cases.surface: `NhAiToolCatalogAttestation.Validate`, `INhAiAttestedToolCatalog.AttestationHash` and the MCP startup validator of `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`
cases.outcome: A runtime catalog that claims attestation is rejected with `InvalidOperationException` before export when it is not `SharedInvoker`-governed, when a created function is not an `INhAiGovernedAIFunction` bound to one of its descriptors (for example a plain function that bypasses `INhAiToolInvoker`), when descriptors, functions and manifest entries disagree, or when the attestation hash differs from the manifest schema hash. cases.title: Assistant conversation with streamed turn
cases.surface: `AddNewHeapAssistant`, `NhAssistantBuilder` (`UsePostgreSql`, `UseSqlServer`, `UseAccessPolicy`, `UseChatProfile`, `AddAgent`, `AddBusinessAuditSink`, `WithLimits`), `NhAssistantAgentDefinition`, `MapNewHeapAssistant`, `NhAssistantOptions` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Enabled`, `AccessPolicy`), the assistant HTTP API and server-sent events, `NhAiScriptedChatClient` (`RespondWithProviderError`)
cases.outcome: The sample registers one agent over the curated `projects.*` tools with a streaming chat profile, PostgreSQL storage in the library-owned `nhai` schema and the `app.active-division.project.view` access policy. A signed-in user creates a conversation and posts a message; the turn streams `turn.started`, a governed `projects.search` call as `tool.started` and `tool.completed` with a bounded result preview, `message.delta` text and `turn.completed` with usage. The tool runs through the shared invoker as the agent on behalf of the accountable user in the active division, the conversation returns to `idle` and its messages and tool-call parts are persisted. The flag, the access policy and the agent's required policy gate every endpoint. A model that sends the search arguments without the `input` envelope still runs the tool once; an envelope mixed with other properties completes that call with `resultCode` `ai-tool-input-invalid`, and the model's corrected retry succeeds in the same turn. When the turn reaches the sample's limit of four tool calls, the fifth call is refused without running, one tool-free model call answers from the four results as `message.delta` and `turn.completed` keeps `assistant-tool-call-limit-reached`; the follow-up turn replays that answer with a bounded `<tool-call-summary>` data block of the executed calls and no result content. A transient provider error inside the model stream (`server_is_overloaded`, `server_error` or `rate_limit_exceeded`) that arrives before any text or tool call is retried once after a short wait; a repeated or other provider error, scripted with `NhAiScriptedChatClient.RespondWithProviderError`, ends the turn as `failed` with `assistant-model-unavailable`, and the failed conversation accepts the next message. By default the sample's deterministic model drives the assistant and every test. Optionally, `SampleProjectManagement:Assistant:Model` in the sample's secrets connects an OpenAI-compatible model under the same keyed client with a larger call budget and timeout; startup fails with a message that names a missing API key or model or an invalid endpoint, never the key itself, and the assistant sends the model's execution region (`external` by default) through `NhAssistantBuilder.UseExecutionRegion`, which the assistant's profile and the planner's triage profiles permit next to `local`.

cases.title: Assistant mutation paused for approval and resumed
cases.surface: Assistant approval flow over `INhAiProposalFactory`, `NhAiApprovalValidator` and the durable `INhAiApprovalEvidenceProvider`, optional `INhAssistantToolPresenter` within `NhAssistantPresentationLimits` (a dropped presentation warns with `NhAssistantPresentationRules`) and presented in every culture of `NewHeap:PlatformAspNetCommon:Settings:SupportedCultures`, `POST conversations/{id}/approvals/{approvalId}/decide`, the `approval.required` event, `INhAssistantBusinessAuditSink` and `NhAssistantAuditEvent`
cases.outcome: When the model calls `projects.change-status`, the shared invoker reports that approval is required before anything executes. The assistant creates the exact NewHeap proposal from the arguments the invoker evaluated, bound to the agent actor, the accountable user, the turn as run, the prompt identity, the tool contract hash and the active-division target; it stores the proposal with a pending approval, streams `approval.required` and pauses the conversation as `waiting-for-approval`. The sample presenter uses those exact arguments and the authorized division to resolve the project server-side and stores a Dutch or English friendly tool name, summary and named old/new status fields beside, never inside, the proposal evidence; missing, failing, oversized or sensitive presentation safely falls back. The selected culture remains stable after reload and resume. The user approves with the expected proposal hash; the same governed function runs again through the invoker with the proposal and approval ids, the validator accepts only that user's decision for that hash within its lifetime, the project status verifier runs and the resumed turn completes. The business audit sink receives content-free `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalApproved` and `ToolInvoked` events. Rejections close without executing and expired proposals end with `assistant-approval-expired`. The presenter keeps within `NhAssistantPresentationLimits`, at most eight fields, so its presentation is never dropped; one that broke a cap would be dropped as a whole with a warning naming the presenter, the tool and the rule, and the approver would read the generic summary. The approval is presented in both supported cultures, so a reader in English reads it in English.

cases.title: Durable assistant budget and idempotency ledgers
cases.surface: Durable `INhAiBudgetManager` on `AssistantBudgetLedger` and `INhAiIdempotencyManager` on `AssistantIdempotencyLease` in the library-owned `nhai` schema, `NhAssistantLimits.DailyToolCallBudgetPerActor`, `NhAssistantBuilder.UseApplicationBudgetInTurns` with `AgentId`, `SkillId`, `RunId` and `Purpose` on `NhAiBudgetRequest` and `NhAiBudgetPurposes`, `NhAssistantDbContextOptions` (`Schema`, `RunMigrations`), provider migrations in `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.SqlServer` and `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.PostgreSql`
cases.outcome: Assistant tool calls are booked atomically per accountable user and UTC day in PostgreSQL; the approved status change takes a durable idempotency lease keyed by its proposal and completes it. When the daily tool budget is exhausted, the next turn ends with the stable `assistant-budget-exhausted` error. Library tests prove the same ledgers, lease expiry takeover with fencing, concurrent reservations that never exceed the budget, the migrations and a configured schema on both SQL Server and PostgreSQL. Outside assistant turns the budget and evidence requests keep using the managers the application registered first. The sample also lets its own budget manager reserve the calls of assistant turns: it reads them as a person's chat with the project assistant, apart from agents' work and MCP clients, counts them per purpose and agent, and keeps bounding the application's own and MCP calls per invocation.

cases.title: Assistant panel in the management portal
cases.surface: `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`: `provideNhAssistant`, `NhAssistantConfig.getStateScope`, `NhAssistantAccessPolicy`, `NhAssistantApiService` (fetch-based SSE), `NhAssistantStore`, `NhAssistantPanelService`, the `nh-assistant-*` launcher, panel, conversation list, thread, composer, tool-call group, tool-call card, approval card and agent picker, `NH_ASSISTANT_ICONS`, and `provideNhAssistantMockApi` from `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/testing`
cases.outcome: The management portal registers the assistant once with the NewHeap session token and an `app.assistant.access` permission policy, shows the launcher in the header and one CDK overlay panel in the layout. The Assistant playground runs the same panel on a scripted mock API: a new conversation streams Markdown answers, consecutive tool calls collapse into one group that names the running tool, counts finished and failed calls and expands to cards with status and translated result codes, a working indicator with elapsed seconds covers the pauses between tool calls, a mutation pauses on a friendly approval card that keeps tool ids, targets and redacted arguments in collapsed technical details and sends the expected proposal hash once for approve or reject, a running turn can be stopped, server errors appear as translated messages, and switching agents starts a new conversation. A turn that fails, such as the playground's unavailable-model prompt, keeps its translated error bar while the composer stays available, and the next message continues the same conversation; a conversation or agent thread whose last turn failed says so when it is reopened and accepts a new message as well, while only an archived conversation is closed. Users can keep typing and submit follow-ups while a turn runs or waits for approval. The panel queues them in FIFO order per conversation, captures their page context, and sends only after the active turn finishes; queues continue in background conversations and clear on account or access changes. Queued messages can be edited or removed without replacing the current draft. Steering prioritizes a correction and waits for confirmed authorized cancellation before sending it in the same conversation. Stop pauses the queue; failures retain unsent messages for explicit resume, without automatically approving tools. The playground has an executable two-message queue demo. Explicit send returns focus, and automatic focus restoration does not steal focus or open a mobile keyboard. Old events without presentation use a localized safe fallback. The launcher disappears when the server reports the assistant disabled or the access policy denies the user, model text never renders HTML or script, and the English and Dutch texts have identical keys. With `getPageContext` each message carries what the user has open, such as the simulated project page of the playground; a page icon above the message box describes it, the user can leave it out of the next message, and a failing getter never blocks sending. The root portal and mock playground provide separate per-user `getStateScope` values: a reload restores the open drawer, selected agent and last conversation through the current session, while a new turn uses only the current page context and inaccessible conversations fall back to a new thread. The assistant picker appears only when more than one assistant is available; a single assistant stays automatically selected and the composer can still send. With multiple assistants it sits in the composer prompt bar beside the send/stop action, keeps capability details in its tooltip and accessible description, and preserves the draft when selecting another agent.

cases.title: End-to-end assistant over bridge and curated tools
cases.surface: `AddSampleAiBridge` before `AddSampleAssistant`, agent `sample-project-assistant` with tool selectors `projects.*` and `sample-api.*`, `POST conversations/{id}/messages` (SSE), `POST conversations/{id}/approvals/{approvalId}/decide`, `POST admin/mcp-servers`, `POST admin/mcp-servers/{id}/sync`, `PUT admin/mcp-servers/{id}/tools/{remoteName}`, `POST admin/agents`, `AddOpenApi("v1")` with `MapOpenApi` next to the bridge and `MapSampleAssistant`
cases.outcome: One assistant conversation combines the API bridge and the curated tools: a division editor's turn calls the bridge tool `sample-api.project.get` (forwarded to the API as the signed-in user with the invocation header) and the curated `projects.search`, both reported as `tool.completed`; a status change pauses with `approval.required`, runs `projects.change-status` after approval and passes its verifier. An administrator connects an MCP server, activates its read-only tool and creates an agent that uses a bridge tool and the MCP tool in one turn. A viewer is offered only read tools (no bridge create/update, no `projects.change-status`), so a mutation attempt produces no approval card and changes nothing. Arguments, results, messages and secrets never reach the business audit sink, the platform audit sink or the logs. The bridge checks its catalog only after the application's endpoints are registered, so the API's OpenAPI document lists the assistant's minimal API endpoints, such as `/api/assistant/conversations`, next to the controller actions the bridge publishes.

cases.title: Administrator-managed assistant agents
cases.surface: `AddAgent` code agents persisted in `AssistantAgent`, `UseAdminPolicy`, `GET/POST admin/agents`, `PUT admin/agents/{id}` with `expectedVersion`, `POST admin/agents/{id}/reset`, `DELETE admin/agents/{id}`, `GET admin/tools`, `AssistantStatus.canAdminister`, `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.AdminAgentCreated|Updated|Deleted|Reset`, `NhAssistantLimits.MaxToolSelectorsPerAgent`
cases.outcome: Code agents are upserted into the library-owned `nhai` schema at startup and remain the default; an administrator can override, disable and reset them without changing their `code` source, and create own agents with a display name, instructions, tool selectors, an optional required policy and an autonomy level. In the sample an administrator creates a read-only portfolio agent; users see it with its literal display name, start a conversation and the agent searches projects with the curated tool while mutating tools stay out of reach. Users without the admin policy receive `403`, every change is versioned (`409` on a stale version) and reported as a content-free audit event. The application decides how many tool selectors an agent may list through `NhAssistantLimits.MaxToolSelectorsPerAgent` (the sample raises the default 128 to 256), bounded by the stored selector length; administrator input above the limit returns 400.

cases.title: Administrator-connected MCP servers assigned to agents
cases.surface: `ConfigureMcp` (`AllowedHosts`, `ForwardUserTokenHosts`, `RequireHttps`, `ToolListCacheDuration`, `ConnectTimeout`, `ReaderCallTimeout`, `MaxResponseBytes`, `MaxToolListPages`, `MaxTools`, `ForwardedTokenLifetime`), `admin/mcp-servers` with `test`, `sync` and tool activation, auth modes `none`, `bearer`, `api-key`, `basic` (`userName`) and `forward-user-token`, `secretReference` with `config:` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:Secrets`) and `INhAssistantMcpSecretResolver` registered with `AddMcpSecretResolver`, `clientCertificateReference` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:ClientCertificates`), `transport` (`streamable-http`, `auto`), `headlessUse` with `NhAssistantMcpHeadlessUses` (`never`, `organization`, `personal`), the caller's consent through `GET` and `PUT mcp-connections`, `AddNewHeapPlatformAIMcpDelegatedTokens` with `Accept` and `INhAiMcpDelegatedTokenIssuer`, the audit kinds `McpBackgroundUseChanged` and `McpDelegatedTokenIssued`, `lastConnectAt` and `lastConnectCode`, the codes `assistant-mcp-insufficient-scope`, `assistant-mcp-headless-not-allowed`, `assistant-mcp-consent-required`, `assistant-mcp-delegated-token-unavailable`, `assistant-mcp-secret-reference-invalid` and `assistant-mcp-certificate-reference-invalid` at runtime and the field error `not-found` for a saved reference that names nothing, `INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`, `INhAiCallerCredentialAccessor`, agent `mcpServerIds`, the server editor in `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/admin` and `nh-assistant-mcp-connections` in the preferences, and asymmetric signing of the host's tokens for first-party servers: `NhJwtSigningKeys` (`Signing:Algorithm` `ES256`, `KeyId` and the private key from the secrets file), `MapNewHeapJwks`, `UseNewHeapJwks` and `INhAuthenticationService.CreateDelegatedTokenAsync` with `audience`; a left-out personal server on the run (`McpConnectionSkips`, `NhAssistantRunMcpSkipDto`, `mcpConnectionSkips` in `nh-assistant-run-result`) and the agent notification `McpConnectionMissing` through `UseInAppAgentNotifications`; an authentication mode of the application: `INhAssistantMcpCredentialProvider` registered with `AddMcpCredentialProvider` (`NhAssistantMcpCredentialOwnership`, `NhAssistantMcpCredentialProviders`), `GET admin/mcp-auth-modes` and the editor's application modes (`McpCustomAuthMode`, `getMcpAuthModes`, the mock's `mcpAuthModes`)
cases.outcome: An administrator connects a Streamable HTTP MCP server with an API key that is protected with ASP.NET Data Protection and never returned, synchronizes its tools, which start disabled as approval-required mutations, activates one tool as read-only and assigns the server to one agent. That agent calls the remote tool through the governed MCP importer and the shared invoker; other agents never see it. A changed remote input schema disables a tool until it is activated again, the user token is forwarded only to allow-listed hosts, link-local, metadata and non-development loopback hosts are blocked after DNS resolution and again at connect time, and an unreachable server is skipped without breaking the turn. A server starts at `headlessUse: never`: the status advisor, working in the background for the participant who started it, is not offered its tools until an administrator allows the server's own API key in background runs; the participant's rights then authorize the call. Every request carries the credential and is checked against the planned origin and the allowed hosts, a test records the connection state, a tool list seen with one caller's token never disables a tool for everyone, and an approved deferred MCP proposal executes once while the server still allows background runs. An administrator can name a secret that the application holds instead of storing it: `config:<name>` reads the dedicated configuration section and `secret-file:<name>` a mounted secret file through the sample's resolver; both are read for every connection, so a rotation applies at once, and a reference never reaches other settings or climbs out of a directory. Basic authentication shows the user name and keeps the password write-only. A first-party server that accepts the person's NewHeap token serves the status advisor in a background run only after the participant allowed it in the preferences: every request then carries a short-lived delegated token of the participant, marked with the invocation and bound to the server's origin, which the server accepts below `/mcp` only and the assistant's own host never accepts; issuing and consent are audited without the token. The sample host of the agent run tests signs its tokens with ES256 and publishes only the public key; the first-party server validates with that key set and cannot mint a token, and every delegated token names the server's origin as `aud`, so the host itself refuses it. A background run that leaves the server out for want of the participant's consent records the server and the reason on the run, and the participant finds the reason in the application's inbox, once a day. The sample adds its own authentication mode that exchanges the person's NewHeap token at the identity provider for a token of the MCP server; administrators choose it like a built-in mode, and the server never sees a person's own token. An approver who decides another person's proposal in an agent thread continues that person's turn in the approver's own request; the turn is headless for the person who asked, so a personal server serves it only with that person's consented delegated token and never with the approver's token or connection, and the sample's token exchange is never asked for the approver's token. The model calls a server's tools by names that keep the server id's dashes, such as mcp_team-calendar_next_milestone, so no two tools of an agent's servers share a name; tools that still would are offered by neither. A stored secret or reference never follows a server to another origin, authentication mode or api-key header: moving the server there needs the secret again. The composition bounds every request to a server: connecting and listing its tools each by the connect timeout, a reader's call by the reader call timeout, a response or one event of its stream by the largest response, read no further, and a tool list by its pages and tools, with assistant-mcp-response-too-large and assistant-mcp-tool-list-too-large beyond them.

cases.title: Editable application context and personal assistant preferences
cases.surface: `UseDefaultApplicationContext`, `GET/PUT admin/context`, `GET admin/context/versions`, `GET/PUT preferences` (`style`, `addressForm`, `responseLength`, `customInstructions`), instruction composition in order of authority, prompt identity in the invocation context and `NhAssistantAuditEvent`
cases.outcome: The sample seeds its application context once as version 1; an administrator edits it with the expected version and a later seed never overwrites the edit. A user stores personal style preferences; the next turn uses library rules, the edited application context, the agent instructions and, last and explicitly bounded, the Dutch style lines and custom instructions chosen from `Accept-Language`. Custom instructions cannot change tools or approvals, and the context and preference texts never reach logs or audit, which carry their versions and hashes instead. Preferences belong to the person a turn works for: when an approver decides another person's proposal in an agent thread, the continued turn composes its prompt from the preferences, custom instructions, situation and name of the person who asked, never from the approver's.

cases.title: Assistant administration and preferences UI
