cases.outcome: From the panel header a user chooses style, form of address and answer length and writes own instructions of at most 1,000 characters; saving, validation and failures are shown in place. When the server reports `canAdminister` and the host configured `adminRoute`, the panel links to the administration page. There an administrator edits the versioned application context and sees a conflict instead of overwriting a newer version, overrides, disables and resets code agents, creates and deletes own agents with tool selectors from the tool catalog and assigned MCP servers, and connects MCP servers with a write-only secret that is never shown, only kept, replaced or cleared. After a sync every remote tool is disabled and treated as a change until the administrator enables it and chooses its effect; remote annotations are shown as hints and a changed remote input schema disables the tool with a warning. The management playground runs all of this on the scripted mock API. Every place that names an agent, the editor's title and the import dialog included, shows an agent in code by its translated name in the reader's language. The administration's English and Dutch texts ship with `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/admin` and merge when one of its components is created, so the portal's initial bundle carries only the texts of the panel and the administration's texts load with its lazy routes. The administration opens on Agents: one list with one status per agent, where it works, where it comes from and what needs attention, searchable and filtered, with each shadow variant below its agent. A row opens the agent's page, whose header holds its status with only the changes it allows now (each with its explanation and an optional reason), "Test in chat", "Run now" and "More" with export, reset to code and delete behind a confirmation. Its tabs follow the agent's life: Overview shows its flow and status, Build one page of sections (profile, tools, skills with their status, triggers, connected agents and guardrails, the latter with what its code sets read only), Rollout everything that is not live yet with the shadow variants and their evaluation, and Activity its runs and feedback. The portal keeps the open agent and its tab in the URL, so a link opens that page and the back button returns step by step. A Chat page in the portal's menu shows the same chat in place for long sessions, with the conversations beside the thread on wide screens.

cases.title: Situational and page context for assistant turns
cases.outcome: Every assistant turn starts with a "Situation" data block: the library's date, weekday and time in Europe/Amsterdam plus the signed-in sample user's name and roles from `SampleAssistantTurnContextProvider`. When the client sends the page it has open, a "User's screen" block lists the route, title and up to five entities. Both blocks follow the instructions, are marked as data rather than instructions, are bounded (20 facts and 2,000 characters; route 200, title 120, five entities) and do not change the prompt hash, so pending approvals stay valid. A page context of the wrong shape is ignored instead of rejecting the message. Audit events carry only the fact and entity counts and whether page context was present.

cases.title: API bridge gateway over read-only resources
cases.outcome: Instead of one tool per action, the sample publishes four read-only gateway tools over the read-only project and project-task resources. Canonical `CollectionRequestModel`, `CollectionResultModel<T>` and `SimpleCollectionResultModel<T>` endpoints need no consumer conventions: NewHeap derives filter, order, search and result metadata from the same `[Filterable]`, `[Orderable]` and `[Searchable]` attributes and operator vocabulary used by collection processing. Resource identifiers remain invariant while localized titles and summaries come from consumer-owned resources with English fallbacks. Discovery reauthorizes controller policies and binds the supplied invocation context to the signed-in actor. `query` and `get` run the underlying bridge descriptor through the shared invoker, so gate, policies, budget, audit and self-HTTP remain unchanged; unsupported fields fail before HTTP, unknown and unauthorized resources remain indistinguishable, and mutations never enter the gateway. The query-string collection endpoint is recognized from its documented canonical result type and uses the same NewHeap wire contract without `SampleAiBridgeConventions`. Gateway results are shaped before the size bound: items are compacted by default, `fields` projects result fields including one dotted level, `countOnly` returns only `totalCount`, e-mail and phone fields are redacted at every depth with `RedactResultFields`, and an oversized page keeps whole items with structured `truncation` guidance instead of a raw `bodyText` fragment. `describe-resource` publishes the fields a search matches as `searchFields`; the project resources search only key, name and description, so their searches reach the API, while a resource that searched a redacted field, or did not say which fields it searches, would refuse a search before the HTTP call and be described as not searchable.

cases.title: Two-factor login challenge
cases.outcome: An account with an enrolled authenticator receives a short-lived, single-use challenge instead of a session after its password or a consumer-specific credential, and an authenticator or recovery code completes it. The challenge is never stored as an authorization in the frontend, wrong codes count towards the lockout, and a used code or challenge cannot be replayed. Password-only accounts, refresh rotation for enrolled users and Microsoft OAuth keep their behavior, while paths that can only return a complete session refuse the account instead of skipping the second factor. The shared sample login shows the challenge component, which lets the user pick a method, and resumes a challenge that is still pending in the tab.

cases.title: Authenticator enrollment and recovery codes
cases.surface: `INhTwoFactorService<TUser>`, the account two-factor endpoints, `BaseNhAuthService.beginAuthenticatorSetup`, `confirmAuthenticator`, `regenerateRecoveryCodes` and `disableTwoFactor`, `NhTwoFactorTestCodes`, `NhTwoFactorSettingsComponent` and `NhTwoFactorRecoveryCodesComponent`
cases.outcome: A signed-in user enrolls an authenticator app from a pending key with a server-rendered QR code and receives single-use recovery codes that are stored as hashes. Confirmation ends every other session and returns a renewed session for this device. Regenerating recovery codes and disabling two-factor authentication require the password or a code, disabling is refused while the policy requires a second factor, and changes are refused while an administrator impersonates the user. The shared profile page manages every factor with the settings component, which asks for the password or a code before sensitive changes and shows new recovery codes once with copy and download actions. Recovery codes are stored as keyed hashes under the two-factor code key, which the sample reads from its secrets file next to the JWT key; unkeyed entries and plaintext codes from earlier versions still redeem once and are rewritten into keyed hashes by the first redemption. Authenticator keys follow the ASP.NET Core Identity default and are stored unprotected; the provider tests show that Identity's personal-data protection protects them while the challenge keeps working.

cases.title: Email verification codes
cases.outcome: A signed-in user confirms the e-mail address as a second factor with an e-mailed code, and a pending challenge can then be completed with a sign-in code sent to that address. Codes are stored as keyed hashes, expire, work once, replace the previous code and respect a resend cooldown; a code sent with an unkeyed hash before the upgrade works until it expires, and a changed e-mail address must be confirmed again. The code notification is created through the NewHeap notification outbox in the same transaction as the stored code. The e-mail's delivery expires with the code, so the notification processor removes the code from the delivery store once the e-mail is sent and never keeps it after the code expired; a composer that sets a later expiry or none is held to the code's lifetime, and delivery data that cannot expire is still sent with a warning and keeps the code until the retention cleanup. The sample renders the e-mail with its Razor mail layout through a custom message composer that sets that expiry, and e-mail codes do not satisfy the security-officer requirement because the mailbox also resets the password.

cases.title: Passkeys
cases.outcome: The sample opts into the ASP.NET Core Identity passkey table with one migration that adds only AspNetUserPasskeys. A signed-in user registers a passkey whose attestation, relying-party domain and origin are verified, then signs in without a username or password with the discoverable passkey or uses it as the second factor after the password. Ceremony state travels in short-lived protected tokens, every ceremony works once, the signature counter is stored, and removing the last second factor disables two-factor authentication unless the policy requires it.

cases.title: Remembered devices
cases.outcome: After a second factor with "remember this device", later password sign-ins on that device skip the second factor for 30 days while the policy allows it. Cookie clients receive the token as an HttpOnly cookie and header clients store it for the realm; the token belongs to one user and to the current security stamp, so forgetting devices, a password change or any two-factor change invalidates every remembered device.

cases.title: Mandatory two-factor policy
cases.outcome: Members of the security-officer role must use a second factor. Without one, the password step returns an enrollment step instead of a session; its token only enrolls an authenticator or a passkey, after which the session and the recovery codes are issued. Until they enroll, their refresh tokens stop working, they cannot disable the factor or remove its last passkey afterwards, and a passkey sign-in satisfies the requirement on its own. Other accounts keep their password-only sign-in.

cases.title: Two-factor administration and security notifications
cases.surface: `NhTwoFactorBuilder.UseAdministrationPolicy`, `UseSecurityNotifications` and `UseMessageComposer`, `INhTwoFactorService<TUser>.ResetAsync`, `NhBackgroundOperationBuilder.AddTwoFactorOperations`, the two-factor administration endpoints, `BaseNhAuthService.resetUserTwoFactor`, `startTwoFactorEnrollmentReminders` and `startTwoFactorSessionRevocation`
cases.outcome: Managers with the two-factor administration permission reset the second factors of a user who lost access to them, which ends every session of that user, and start background operations that remind unenrolled security officers or end their sessions so the next sign-in enrolls them, with progress and idempotency keys. Users receive in-app and e-mail security notifications for enabled and disabled factors, new recovery codes, used recovery codes, lockouts, passkey changes and resets; each notification is created in the same transaction as the change and uses the English or Dutch texts.

cases.title: Shared assistant conversations with read state and live updates
cases.surface: `POST conversations/{id}/share-link` and `DELETE`, `POST conversations/{id}/join`, `GET conversations/{id}/participant-candidates`, `POST conversations/{id}/participants`, `DELETE conversations/{id}/participants/{actorId}`, `POST conversations/{id}/read`, `INhAssistantParticipantDirectory` with `UseParticipantDirectory`, `INhAssistantDisplayNameResolver`, `NhAssistantLimits.MaxParticipantsPerConversation`, `NhAssistantOptions.HubPath` (mapped on the host's root outside the route prefix, with the query token read for the configured path), the `NhAssistantHub` SignalR hub (`ConversationChanged`, `ConversationRead`, `ConversationRemoved`, `ConversationEvent`), the conversation fields `role`, `members`, `currentActorId`, `activeActorId`, `lastMessageSequence` and `lastReadSequence`, and `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.Conversation*`
cases.outcome: An owner shares a conversation through an invitation link whose token is protected with ASP.NET Data Protection, or invites a colleague of the active division through the sample's `SampleAssistantParticipantDirectory`. A colleague of the same tenant who may use the agent joins, sees the whole history as read and continues the conversation: the turn runs with the colleague's own permissions, budget and approval, the model receives every user message with its writer's name and a shared-conversation data block, and only the person whose turn created a proposal can decide it while the owner or that person can stop the turn. Each user message records its author; owner and participants keep their own read position, which only moves forward and marks the other person's answer as unread. The owner removes participants, renews or revokes the link and deletes the conversation for everyone; a participant leaves. Every change is a content-free audit event, and the SignalR hub sends status, read and removal updates and the streamed turn events to the owner and current participants only. The hub decides every update with the read rule of the conversation's snapshot at the moment it sends it: a participant receives a chat only while the person, as the platform rebuilds them, passes the agent's policy, and only on connections signed in for the chat's tenant; an agent thread reaches people whose role on the subject holds or who were invited, also when an old participant row still names someone whose role ended. A connection closes when the token it was opened with expires and when the session validator no longer accepts it, such as after a password change, and deleting a person removes their participant rows. Conversations from before sharing keep working as read. The hub maps on the host's root at `/hub/assistant`, outside the `/api/assistant` prefix; NewHeap's bearer setup reads the WebSocket's query token for the configured hub path, so a hub moved to `/hubs/assistant` keeps connecting, while no other request takes a token from the query string.

cases.title: Assistant Web Push notifications for longer turns
cases.surface: `NhAssistantBuilder.ConfigurePush`, `NhAssistantPushOptions` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Push`: `PublicKey`, `PrivateKey`, `Subject`, `AllowedEndpointHosts`, `MinimumTurnDuration`, `IncludeConversationTitle`, `TimeToLive`), `NhAssistantWebPushKeys.Generate`, `GET/PUT notifications`, `PUT/DELETE notifications/push-subscription` (`403 assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating` for a registration in an impersonation session), the bundled `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/push/nh-assistant-push-worker.js` and `NhAssistantConfig.push`
cases.outcome: With VAPID keys the server offers Web Push; the sample creates a key pair per run in Development and reads keys from configuration elsewhere. Notifications are on by default and each user can turn them off for all devices. A browser registers a subscription only for an allowed push service over https, so the server never posts to an address a client chose. An impersonation session registers no browser for the person it acts as, because the browser would keep receiving the person's notifications after the session ended (`403 assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating`); removing a subscription stays allowed. When a turn that ran at least the minimum duration finishes or fails, the owner and participants get an RFC 8291 encrypted, VAPID-signed notification with the conversation title and a short localized status; an approval notifies only the person who decides it, and cancelled or quick turns stay silent. Notifications never contain messages or tool data. A notification reaches only the people the conversation's read rule admits when it is sent, and nobody the platform no longer resolves, such as a deleted, blocked or locked-out account. Deleting a person through NewHeap Identity removes their browser subscriptions, notification choice, MCP connection notices and conversation rows through the assistant's retention participant. The worker shows a notification only while no window of the application is focused and opens the conversation on click. Subscriptions the push service reports as gone are removed.

cases.title: Parallel and shared conversations in the assistant panel
cases.surface: `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`: `NhAssistantStore` sessions (`activity`, `runningCount`, `unreadCount`, `members`, `canDecide`, `activeMember`, `joinConversation`, `createShareLink`, `inviteParticipant`, `removeParticipant`, `setViewing`), `nhAssistantIsUnread`, `NhAssistantLiveService`, `NhAssistantPushService`, `nh-assistant-activity`, `nh-assistant-share`, the launcher badge, the notification bell in `nh-assistant-panel`, `NhAssistantShareComponent.section` and the notification setting in `nh-assistant-preferences`, `NhAssistantConfig.liveUpdates`, `hubBaseUrl`, `buildShareLink`, the `#nh-assistant-join` and `#nh-assistant-conversation` fragments, and `NhAssistantMockLiveService` with `NhAssistantMockBackend.simulateParticipantTurn` from `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/testing`
cases.outcome: Several conversations run at the same time: starting or opening another conversation never stops a running turn. A slim row below the panel header appears only when another conversation works, waits for approval or has an unread answer, and selecting a chip opens it; the launcher shows one badge for a waiting approval, the number of unread conversations or a running turn, and the conversation list marks the same states. The open conversation counts as read only while the drawer shows it in a visible, focused window. Separate link and people icons above the composer open the invitation-link and participant views. The owner shares with a copyable invitation link and, when the server offers a directory, a colleague search; participants see who takes part and can leave. In a shared conversation messages of other people show their names, their turns and answers arrive live, the composer says who is working and an approval of someone else's turn shows who decides instead of the buttons. Opening an invitation link joins and opens the conversation and removes the token from the address bar. A bell in the panel header turns desktop notifications on or off when available, indicates off or blocked states and reports update failures; the preferences also explain the browser state; the browser asks for permission on the next message sent. The management playground demonstrates parallel prompts and a simulated colleague on the scripted mock API with in-memory live updates, and the portal registers live updates through `/api/hub/assistant` and Web Push with the bundled worker.

cases.title: Assistant context for a reviewed MCP tool
cases.surface: `AddMcpContextBinding` with `NhAssistantMcpContextBinding` (server id, URL and remote tool name, `IncludeSnapshot`, `Snapshot`), `NhAssistantMcpContext.MetaKey` (`com.newheap/assistant-context`), `INhAssistantConversationSnapshotProvider`, `NhAssistantConversationSnapshotRequest`, `NhAssistantConversationSnapshot`, `NhAssistantSnapshotCodes` and the generic `INhAiMcpInvocationBinder`
cases.outcome: A research MCP tool that an administrator connected under the reviewed server id and URL receives, in the request metadata, the acting agent, the accountable person, the conversation, turn and tool invocation ids, approval and proposal ids after an approval, and a bounded snapshot with the first question and the latest completed user and assistant text; its model-facing schema only asks for the question. The same tool under another server id or URL receives nothing. The snapshot refuses calls outside the running tool call, another person, another invocation or run and a stale turn, leaves out output of the running turn, also after an approval pause, and reports omitted messages and bytes.

cases.title: Batch media file lookup
cases.outcome: A view that references many media files collects their ids and resolves them with one call: SQL Server and PostgreSQL read the files with one primary-key query and their distinct folders with one lookup-index query, instead of two queries per file, and very large sets use fixed-size batches. Duplicate ids are ignored, missing ids are reported separately and thumbnails are filled. A lookup by path reads the file and its folder id in one round trip. Both providers keep every lookup on an index seek. Custom storage and media services without a batch implementation fall back to one lookup per id.

cases.title: Event-triggered agent run with deferred proposals
cases.surface: `NhAssistantBuilder.AddAgent`, `ConfigureAgent` with `Grant`, `TriggerOnly`, `UseApprovalPolicy`, `Retry` and `Budget`, `AddApprovalPolicy` with `NhAiApprovalMode.Deferred`, `NhAiApprovers.SubjectRole`, `FourEyes` and `RequireUnchangedSubject`, `AddTrigger<TEvent>` with `StartAgent`, `Subject`, `Initiator`, `Message`, `Dedupe` and `OnBusy`, `INhAssistantAgentTriggers.PublishAsync`, `NhAiToolAttribute.AllowAgentGrant`, `NhBackgroundOperationBuilder.AddAssistantAgentRuns`, `GET threads/{id}/runs`, `GET threads/{id}/proposals`, `GET approvals/inbox` and `POST approvals/{id}/decisions`; for the application's own channels `INhAssistantProposalDecisionService` with `GetDecisionFactsAsync` (`NhAssistantProposalDecisionFacts` with `SubjectChanged`) and `DecideAsync` (`NhAssistantDecidingPerson`, `NhAssistantProposalDecision`, `NhAssistantProposalDecisionResult` with `Duplicate`), `NhAssistantDecisionChannels` and the `Channel` and `IdempotencyKey` of `NhAssistantAuditEvent`
cases.outcome: Creating a project starts the intake reviewer from the sample's CAP consumer after the project transaction committed. The run is a background operation owned by the agent, not by the person who created the project; the agent answers for its own runs and may propose `projects.change-status` because both the tool (`AllowAgentGrant`) and the agent registration grant it, for trigger runs only. The deferred proposal waits in the project's agent thread and in the approval inbox: people outside the project do not see the thread, the creator may not approve it (four eyes), and a project approver who satisfies the tool's manage policy approves it. The approved proposal then executes as its own background operation and changes the project status once. An approver may also answer with a messaging reply: the sample's channel asks the decision service whether a person may decide before it sends them a reply token (the creator and someone outside the project are not asked), and the provider delivers the reply to `POST approval-replies`, where the channel rebuilds the person from the user store and decides as them with the checks of the decision endpoint. A forged token or an unclear answer decides nothing, a reply the provider delivers twice returns the earlier decision, another answer afterwards is refused as not pending, and the audit records the `messaging-reply` channel and the delivery id, where the endpoint records `web`.

cases.title: At-least-once event delivery starts one agent run
cases.outcome: The outbox may deliver `ProjectCreatedEvent` more than once. The trigger keys each delivery by the event id, so the sample's consumer can process the same event repeatedly and the project's agent thread still holds one run; a later publish of the event returns a deduplicated receipt that names that run.

cases.title: Project members decide access to agent threads
cases.surface: `INhAiSubjectAccessResolver` (`DescribeAsync`, `ResolveAsync`, `ListMembersAsync`), `NhAiSubjectInfo`, `NhAiSubjectRole`, `NhAssistantBuilder.AddSubjectType`, `INhAiSubjectAccess.RefreshAsync`, `GET threads` and the `ProjectMember` entity, service and `project-members` endpoints
cases.outcome: `ProjectSubjectAccessResolver` maps project members to reader, participant and approver and treats the project owner as approver. Readers see a project's agent thread but cannot decide its proposals, participants cannot decide them either, and approvers can. `ProjectMemberService` accepts only people of the project's division, once per project, and refreshes the thread's member snapshot after every change. Because the assistant asks the resolver on every request, a removed member loses access to the thread at once. The refresh after a removal also removes the participant row the former member's reading created, so no live update or notification of the thread names them, while live updates and notifications ask the resolver when they are sent either way.

cases.title: An agent proposal for an edited subject closes as stale at the decision or before execution
cases.outcome: The intake reviewer's proposal records the project version it was made for. When the project is edited before an approver decides, the decision facts report `SubjectChanged`, which the messaging channel passes on, and an approval is refused with `assistant-proposal-stale` and closes the proposal as stale at once, by the same precondition the execution runs. When the project is edited after an approval, the execution operation checks the version first and closes the proposal as stale without changing the project.

cases.title: Inline approval that suspends and resumes a headless agent run
cases.outcome: A project participant starts the status advisor on a project. Its status proposal follows the `project-status-inline` policy: the run stops as `waiting-for-approval`, and its background operation releases the worker as `WaitingForSignal` instead of holding a request or a thread. When the participant approves, the decision signals the operation, the run resumes in the same turn, changes the status itself and completes. Nothing changes before the decision. When nobody decides, the proposal expires after the policy's four hours on the application's clock, which the suspended operation waits on as well: the test host moves its registered `TimeProvider` past those hours instead of waiting, the run fails with `assistant-approval-expired` and the failure class `policy` without a change, as the policy's `OnExpiry(FailRun)` says, and a later decision is refused. Whether the maintenance job or the woken operation expires the proposal first, the operation ends the run by the policy, once. When the waiting run's background operation ends without it instead, because an operator cancelled it in the administration, reconciliation failed it as `dispatch-stalled` or a worker failed it on its payload, the maintenance job ends the run once the operation has been terminal for the stale timeout of real time: cancelled with `assistant-run-operation-cancelled`, or failed with `assistant-run-operation-stalled` or `assistant-run-operation-ended`, its inline proposal withdrawn and its thread free for the agent's next run (library evidence on both providers).

cases.title: An agent run with the rights of the person who started it
cases.outcome: The status advisor has no grants of its own. In the background, without a request, the platform builds the starting participant's principal from the user manager's current claims and authorizes the tool's policies against the project's division, so the advisor can propose exactly what that person could do; the proposal records the grant source `delegated` and the participant as initiator. A reader of the project cannot start the advisor. A participant lends rights only to their own requests: a turn of the advisor's run that answers a message another member typed while it worked does not delegate from the participant who started it.

cases.title: Approved agent proposal with an unknown outcome resolved by a person
cases.surface: `NhAiToolEffect.Mutation` with `AllowAgentGrant`, the `nh-ai-execute-proposal-once` operation, `NhAssistantApprovalStatuses.ExecutionUnknown` and `Resolved`, and `POST approvals/{id}/resolve`
cases.outcome: `projects.request-review` sends a new review request on every call, so an approved proposal for it executes in a background operation that never retries. When the call fails without a result, the request may or may not have reached the review board: the proposal becomes `execution-unknown` instead of failed, nothing runs it again, and an approver confirms the outcome with `mark-resolved` (or runs it again with `re-execute`). The tool sends a request only for a project of the division its call is authorized for; a project of another division is refused with project-out-of-division-scope before anything reaches the review board.

cases.title: Webhook, schedule and kill switch for an agent
cases.surface: `NhAssistantBuilder.AddWebhookTrigger` with `Secret`, `Subject` and `Message`, `POST {prefix}/triggers/{id}` with `X-NH-Timestamp`, `X-NH-Delivery` and `X-NH-Signature`, `AddScheduledTrigger` with `Cron`, `Subjects`, `MaxSubjectsPerTick` and `OnBusy`, `POST admin/agents/{id}/kill-switch`, `NhAssistantKillSwitchDto`, `INhAssistantAgentNotificationPolicy`, `INhAssistantAgentNotificationChannel` and `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.AgentTriggerAccepted`, `AgentTriggerRejected`, `AgentRunEnded`, `AgentProposalExecuted`, `AgentProposalResolved` and `AdminAgentRunsStopped`
cases.outcome: The review board answers a review request with a webhook call signed over its timestamp, delivery id and body; a forged signature is refused, a repeated delivery returns the run it started, also a delivery that joined a pending run or waited for a paused agent once a run took it, as the library tests prove on SQL Server and PostgreSQL, and only a project id and a known verdict from the untrusted body reach the agent. Every Monday at seven a Hangfire recurring job reviews the active projects whose deadline falls within a week, at most 50 per tick and skipping projects with an active run. An administrator engages the intake reviewer's kill switch, which disables it, cancels its active runs and makes new triggers fail with `assistant-agent-disabled`, and releases it again; people without the administrator policy cannot. Triggers, ended runs, executions and kill-switch use are content-free audit events, and the subject's approvers are notified of waiting proposals, reminders, escalations, unknown outcomes and failed runs, never of shadow work. The review board's secret comes from the sample's secrets.json (read with `NhConfigurationSecrets.Read` under the `Secrets` prefix; a setting of the key itself wins), and an unresolved `${Secrets:...}` reference never counts as a secret.

cases.title: Working memory, run summaries, files and redaction of an agent thread
cases.surface: `NhAssistantAgentRunBuilder.Memory<TMemory>`, the internal `memory_get` and `memory_update` functions with JSON Merge Patch, `INhAssistantAgentMemoryMigrator` and `NhAssistantBuilder.UseAgentMemoryMigrator`, `NhAssistantLimits.MaxRunSummaries` and `MaxArtifactBytes`, `INhAiArtifacts.SaveAsync`, `ListAsync` and `GetAsync`, `GET threads/{id}/memory`, `GET threads/{id}/artifacts`, `GET threads/{id}/artifacts/{artifactId}/content`, `NhAssistantThreadMemoryDto`, `NhAssistantArtifactDto`, the `grantSource` and `restricted` fields of tool parts and `INhAiSubjectRetention.ForgetSubjectAsync`; `INhAiSubjectRetention.ForgetSubjectAsync(subject, scopeKey)` with the scope key its resolver described (the unscoped overload is obsolete) and `ProjectSubjects.ScopeKeyOf`
cases.outcome: The intake reviewer keeps its checks and last verdict per project in a working memory that must fit `ProjectIntakeMemory`; a patch that does not fit, is larger than 16 KB or lost a race is refused without changing the memory. The `projects.draft-intake-note` tool saves an intake note as a versioned Markdown file of the thread. The next run starts with the memory, the summaries of the last three runs and the names and versions of the files in an `<agent-continuity>` block; a run stores its summary in the same write that ends it, so a run that reads as ended always has one. Results the agent obtained with its own grant are shown only to people who satisfy the tool's policy; others see that a result is restricted. With client credentials the host's own client obtains a token on first use and reuses it; the planning server sees the sample's client, never a person. With an organization connection the administrator authorizes the organization's account once in a popup: the callback checks the state, the issuer and PKCE, exchanges the code and hands a one-time completion code to the administrator's page, which completes the connection with the administrator's own session; nobody else can complete it. cases.title: A deployment whose rights come from its claims transformation lets agents work outside a request with the rights the application recorded at each person's last request, only while they are fresh
cases.surface: `INhAiAccessSource.GetAsync(actorId, subject)` with `NhAiAccessContext` (`Claims`, `ValidAt`, `IsPersonsOwnRequest`); `NhAiAspNetBuilder.UsePrincipalsFromAccessSource<TSource>` with `NhAiAccessSourceOptions` (`MaxAge`, required and positive, `NameClaimType`, `RoleClaimType`), which replaces the built-in `INhAiPrincipalFactory` of the NewHeap user store and refuses a principal factory of the host's own at registration and at startup; a principal with exactly the source's claims, of authentication type `nh-ai-delegation`, and none without a context, for a context older than `MaxAge` on the application's clock, or whose tenant claim does not name the subject's tenant where tenants come from a claim; every decision outside a request through `INhAiPrincipalFactory`: agent runs that delegate from their initiator and their follow-up runs, consultations, the account an agent answers to, MCP connections in the background and the whole application's people; headless gateway reads, whose `INhAiDelegatedReadCredentialIssuer` is asked only while the factory builds the person's principal; the MCP owner sweep, which removes no connection on the access source's answer
cases.outcome: A deployment for one customer, whose people sign in at the customer's identity provider, adds their rights in its own claims transformation at every request, so the NewHeap user store cannot rebuild them for background work. SampleAccessSourceComposition records the claims of each person's own signed-in requests after the transformation, under the platform's actor id and with the time on the application's clock, in the application's own SampleAccessContexts, and registers it as the AI integration's access source with a maximum age of half an hour; NewHeap stores none of it. A request that an agent's delegated read token or delegated MCP token authenticated, and an impersonation session, are not the person's own (`NhAiAccessContext.IsPersonsOwnRequest`): they keep the date and claims of the person's last own request, so an agent that reads for the manager every twenty minutes still loses the manager's rights half an hour after the manager's own last request, and after sign-out its next read brings nothing back. The principal factory also refuses a context that holds such a marker, and a headless gateway read asks the host's delegated read issuer for a credential only while the factory builds the person's principal from a fresh context, so an issuer that would issue for anyone it knows reads nothing for a person who signed out or whose rights are too old (`api-bridge-unauthenticated`). A run the manager started on a project delegates from the manager and may change the project's status with the rights of the manager's last request, and an agent that acts with the rights of the project's responsible person uses the same record. The colleague, whose rights do not include managing projects, and someone the application never saw are refused with ai-tool-agent-not-granted. Half an hour after the manager's last request, which the test reaches by moving the application's clock instead of waiting, the run is no longer offered the status tool and a call is refused; the manager's next request makes it work again, and the manager's own sign-out request, at the host's sign-out path, forgets the rights at once, while signing out of an impersonation session of the manager does not. The sample's own API signs in with the NewHeap user store, whose built-in principal factory keeps rebuilding its people, so the composition is shown in a focused test.

The task is saved again and the next shadow run finds the same finding: within the proposal's seven-day lifetime the shadow proposal counts as open, as a live one would, so nothing new is recorded, the rules receive `AlreadyOpen` and the audit records `AgentProposalDeduplicated`. cases.title: A durable cancellation that a handler sees before the heartbeat ends the operation cancelled
cases.surface: `INhBackgroundOperationContext.ThrowIfCancellationRequestedAsync`, `INhBackgroundOperationService.RequestCancellationAsync`, `RunStepAsync` of `INhBackgroundOperationProgressContext` and `INhBackgroundOperationStepContext`, `TaskResult.Failed` and `NhBackgroundOperationRetryResult.Retry` with the `FailureCode` and `FailureMessageKey` of `NhBackgroundOperation`, the statuses `Cancelled` and `TimedOut` of `NhBackgroundOperationStatus`, and an error that `INhBackgroundOperationHandler<TRequest>.ExecuteAsync` throws outside a step
cases.outcome: The sample's project-analysis child checks `ThrowIfCancellationRequestedAsync` before every pass. When its owner cancels, it stops at the next pass, and the operation ends `Cancelled` with failure code `cancelled` although no heartbeat ran during the attempt. Only a soft time-out that fired ends an operation `TimedOut`, and the durable check is fenced on the attempt, so a cancellation requested for another attempt does not count for this one. A failed or retry result whose failure code is longer than its column of 100 characters, or whose message key is longer than its column of 300, still completes its attempt, terminally or with its retry, as `handler-rejected` with the generic failure key, and the returned text reaches the operational log only. A step whose action threw keeps its own exception, a cancellation included, when the write that records the step fails; that failure is logged with the operation and attempt, while a lost fence, lock contention and a durable cancellation request that the write finds after the step's own error still stop the attempt, so the operation ends cancelled instead of retrying an error its owner cancelled. After its passes the child stores its analysis in `ProjectAnalysisArchive`, the sample's stand-in for another system, outside a step; the archive's client reports a cancelled call as an error of its own, and the handler lets it travel. When the owner cancels during that call, the heartbeat cancels it, and the operation, which may retry three times, still ends `Cancelled` with its single attempt instead of `handler-failed` with a retry. The runner's failure path checks the fenced durable cancellation of the attempt for every error thrown outside a step: when it is requested the operation ends `Cancelled`, or `TimedOut` when the soft time-out fired first, the error is logged as a warning and nothing retries it, while a lost fence and contention the heartbeat recorded still win, and an error without a request stays `handler-failed` with its retries. The library tests prove the column limits, the step recording and the failure path on SQL Server and PostgreSQL, next to the cancellation and time-out classification.

cases.title: Agent runs keep reserved slots on a queue of their own, and the application finds the run a trigger event started and reads its facts
cases.surface: `AddAssistantAgentRuns(runs => runs.Queue(...).MaxConcurrency(...))` with `NhAssistantAgentRunOperationsBuilder`, `NhBackgroundOperationBuilder.WithReservedQueueConcurrency` and `NhBackgroundOperationsOptions.ReservedQueueConcurrency` within `WithGlobalConcurrency`; `NhAssistantTriggerReceipt.InputId`, `INhAssistantAgentRunLookup.FindByEventAsync` and `FindByInputAsync` with `NhAssistantTriggerEventRun`; `INhAssistantAgentRunLookup.FindRunAsync` with `NhAssistantAgentRunFacts` and `GET agent-maintenance/intake-reviews/{eventId}/run`; `NhAssistantOptions.RunSchedules` for a host that knows the schedules but does not run them
cases.outcome: The sample's assistant operations (agent runs, proposal executions, revalidations, deferred trigger fires and replays) work on the queue `agent-runs`, which keeps two of the eight slots of the global limit for itself and may run four operations at the same time: other work never takes the reserved slots, agent work takes free shared slots once its own are in use, and it leaves the rest of the shared slots to the other work. When a project is created, the intake reviewer's receipt names the queued input that holds the event, and the maintenance page finds the review by the event's id: the input, the run it started and, once the run claimed it, that run's status; a redelivered event finds the review of its first delivery. The page then reads the review run's facts by its id: its agent, project, thread, trigger and its kind, status, failure, attempt, proposal count, summary and result, as the owner's runs view shows them, without reading the assistant's tables. The library tests prove the reservation on SQL Server and PostgreSQL, the lookup for started, coalesced, deduplicated, waiting and deferred fires with a tenant mismatch, the run facts of a queued and an ended run, an unknown run, another tenant's run and the whole application's run for the single tenant, and a host with `RunSchedules` false that starts without Hangfire and adds or removes no recurring job.

cases.title: A person approves an equipment order in their own chat and the order desk reports into that chat
cases.surface: `NhAssistantBuilder.ExecuteInApplication(toolId, reportWithin, configure)` with `NhAssistantApplicationExecutionBuilder.AlsoInline`; `NhAssistantProposalHandOff.Inline`; the tool result `assistant-proposal-handed-to-application`; `INhAssistantProposalExecutionReports.ReportExecutionAsync` posting into a person's chat in the UI culture of the turn that approved the hand-off (`AssistantApproval.DecisionCulture`, the ApprovalCulture migrations for SQL Server and PostgreSQL), the default request culture without a supported one; the report deadline of an inline hand-off in the run maintenance; `POST conversations/{id}/approvals/{approvalId}/resolve` with `NhAssistantResolveExecutionRequest` and `NhAssistantApprovalPartDto.CanResolve`, `ExecutionResultCode` and `ExecutionReportDueAt`; `ApprovalPart.canResolve`, `ApprovalResolution`, `ResolveApprovalRequest`, `NhAssistantApiService.resolveApproval`, `NhAssistantStore.resolveApproval` and the approval card's `resolve` of `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`
cases.outcome: SampleEquipmentOrderComposition declares the order tool with `AlsoInline`, so a person who asks the project assistant in their own chat to order equipment and approves the card hands the order to the order desk instead of running the tool's function. cases.title: The operations code assigns an MCP server to an agent, finds who uses a text asset and compares a shipped package with the host through the assistant's services
cases.surface: `INhAssistantMcpServers` (`ListAsync`, `CreateAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `TestAsync`, `SyncAsync`, `ListToolsAsync`, `UpdateToolAsync`, `AssignAsync`, `UnassignAsync`) with `NhAssistantMcpServerRequest`, `NhAssistantMcpOAuthRequest`, `NhAssistantMcpReaderRequest`, `NhAssistantMcpToolSettingsRequest` and `NhAssistantMcpServerLimits`, returning `NhAssistantMcpServerDto`, `NhAssistantMcpToolDto` and `NhAssistantMcpServerTestResultDto`; the audit kind `AdminMcpServerAssignmentChanged` (`assigned`, `unassigned`) next to `AdminMcpServerCreated`, `AdminMcpServerUpdated`, `AdminMcpServerDeleted`, `AdminMcpServerSynced` and `AdminMcpToolUpdated`; the field error `mcpServerIds: too-long`; `NhAssistantMcpOptions.AllowLoopback` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:AllowLoopback`), refused at start in Production; `INhAssistantInstructionAssetUsage.ListAsync` with `NhAssistantInstructionAssetUsageDto`, `NhAssistantInstructionAssetSkillUseDto` and `NhAssistantInstructionAssetAgentUseDto` and the field error `assetId: invalid`; `INhAssistantAgentPackages.GetPackageAsync` with `NhAssistantInstalledAgentPackageDto` and `NhAssistantPackageAgentLinksDto`, and `INhAssistantAgentPackages.ReadAsync`
cases.outcome: SampleAssistantOperationsService is the sample's operations code. It connects the milestones MCP server through INhAssistantMcpServers instead of the administration's endpoints or the tables: the API key is protected with Data Protection and never returned, the synced lookup tool is enabled as read-only, and the server is assigned to the status advisor. cases.title: A person continues a chat and approves its proposal from a messaging app, and turns outlive a closed browser
cases.outcome: A signed-in person links one of their chats with the project assistant to a messaging app through `POST assistant-channel/links`, which issues a link token for the chat, the person and their active division. The messaging provider delivers the person's messages to `POST assistant-channel/messages` and their answer to an approval card to `POST assistant-channel/decisions` with that token and without a sign-in. `SampleAssistantMessagingChannel` vouches for the person because only the token it issued says who writes: it rebuilds their principal from the user store, as their sign-in would, and runs each turn through `INhAssistantConversationTurns`. The turn is the endpoint's turn with its access rules: the person's conversation, the assistant's access policy and the agent's policy. It runs in the person's active division with the person's own rights for every tool, without a request of the person and without the provider's request around it, so the search reads the person's division and the status change waits for the person's own approval card, which the answer carries with its proposal hash. A `yes` approves and the project's status changes once; an unclear answer, a forged token and a delivery the provider repeats (`assistant-message-duplicate`) start nothing, and a link to someone else's chat finds nothing (`assistant-conversation-not-found`). The audit records the `messaging-chat` channel on the turn's events. A link is a credential of the person, so only the person's own session issues one: an impersonation session gets `403 assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating`, because the link would act as the person after the impersonation ended. Every link carries a digest of the person's security stamp, so a password change or a revocation of the person's sessions ends all the person's links (`sample-assistant-channel-delivery-invalid`) until the person links again. The turn keeps running when the provider's webhook gives up, and the portal shows the same chat. In Development the sample also sets `KeepTurnsAfterDisconnect`, so closing the browser no longer cancels a person's turn: it completes, its tools authorize the principal captured when it started, and the client reloads the chat. The library tests prove both on SQL Server and PostgreSQL: a disconnected turn completes with its tool authorized for the captured principal, is cancelled without the option and still stops on `POST cancel`; the service sends and decides, refuses a person outside the chat, without the access or the agent's policy, of another actor or tenant than the principal, and lets the person's policy, not the request around the call, decide a tool.

cases.title: A person chats with the planner, whose model loads one of its skills with that skill's instructions and tools
cases.surface: `NhAssistantAgentRunBuilder.SkillsInChat` and `NhAssistantAgentRunOptions.SkillsInChat`; `use_skill` in a person's chat without triage, within the person's rights; the skill's `Instructions`, `Tools`, `UseProfile`, `DataClassification`, file limits and `MaxTokensPerRun` in a chat turn; `NhAssistantMessageDto.SkillId` and `skillId` of `Message` in `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`
cases.outcome: SampleProjectPlannerComposition lets people who chat with the planner reach its skills (`SkillsInChat`). A chat turn starts without a skill and offers `use_skill` with the planner's active live skills; asked which task comes next, the model loads the task follow-up skill, without a triage call, and continues with the skill's instructions and only the status tool the skill selects, with the person's own rights. The planner's message of the turn names the skill (`skillId`), and the next turn starts without one. Triage, the skill's daily budget and every other routing stay with runs. cases.title: The status advisor asks which status a project gets, and only the person it asks answers
cases.surface: `NhAssistantAgentRunBuilder.AllowQuestions` and `NhAssistantAgentRunOptions.AllowQuestions`; the governed `ask_question` with `NhAssistantQuestionLimits`; `POST conversations/{id}/questions/{questionId}/answer` with `NhAssistantAnswerQuestionRequest`; `NhAssistantQuestionPartDto` (`question` parts, `NhAssistantConversationDto.PendingQuestion`) with `NhAssistantQuestionStatuses`; the stream events `question.asked` and `question.answered`; `NhAssistantToolCallStatuses.AwaitingAnswer`; the codes `assistant-question-invalid`, `assistant-question-not-found`, `assistant-question-not-pending`, `assistant-question-forbidden`, `assistant-question-expired`, `assistant-question-cancelled` and `assistant-question-answer-invalid`; `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.QuestionAsked`, `QuestionAnswered` and `QuestionExpired`; `nh-assistant-question-card`, `QuestionPart`, `NhAssistantApiService.answerQuestion`, `NhAssistantStore.answerQuestion`, `canAnswer` and the mock API's `question` step in `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`
cases.outcome: SampleStatusAdvisorComposition lets the status advisor ask structured questions in people's chats (`AllowQuestions`). Asked to change the status of a project, the advisor asks which status it should get with the choices Active, On hold and Closed; the turn waits as for an approval, the chat shows the question with `pendingQuestion`, and the audit records whom it asks. A colleague in the shared chat sees the question read-only and is refused with `403 assistant-question-forbidden` when they answer; the person whose turn asked answers On hold, and the turn continues with the answer as the result of the advisor's call. The question then reads as answered with the chosen index. In the management playground the panel shows the question card with one button per choice on the mock API. The library tests prove on SQL Server and PostgreSQL that a question waits and resumes with its answer, that another participant is refused and the answer then continues with the rights of the person who answered, that a question expires with the approval lifetime on the application's clock and releases the conversation, that stopping the turn cancels it, that a question out of bounds is not posted and that an agent without the opt-in offers no `ask_question`; the Angular specs prove the card, the reducer and the mock API in English and Dutch.

cases.title: A structured-output schema that a strict provider accepts, and a model call past its deadline as a failed result
cases.outcome: ProjectAiStatusDigestService asks the governed project model for a structured status digest. Its schema comes from ProjectAiStructuredOutput, the sample's own normalization: Microsoft.Extensions.AI generates it with closed objects and every property required, and the at-risk list's reference into the on-track list's items moves into `$defs`. A deterministic model with `StrictStructuredOutput` accepts the normalized schema and the digest parses, while the schema as `ChatResponseFormat.ForJsonSchema` generates it is refused with HTTP 400, as a provider in strict mode refuses it. A digest whose call passes the run's deadline returns the failed result `ai-model-timeout` instead of throwing. The library tests cover the strict rules for repeated types, referenced arrays, nullable objects and recursive definitions, and the timeout for calls and streams.

cases.title: The project handbook reads a bundle of untrusted Markdown documents with relative links and diagrams

Their text is untrusted: inline HTML shows as text, and a javascript: link or a path outside the bundle shows as its label without a link, while https: and mailto: links open in a new tab. cases.title: The intake reviewer in shadow replaces its open order of the same item, as it would live
cases.surface: Shadow proposals under the approval policy's rule for a newer proposal for the same objects: the guard keys of `INhAiProposalGuard.GetKeysAsync` stored for shadow proposals too (`AssistantApprovalKey`, no migration); `NhAiDuplicateProposals.Supersede`, `Skip` and `Allow` among an agent's shadow proposals in its shadow threads of the scope within their proposal lifetime, after the identity rule of SPM-324 and without the rejection cooldown; `NhAssistantApprovalStatuses.ShadowSuperseded` (`shadow-superseded`) with `supersededByApprovalId`, `NhAssistantApprovalStatuses.IsShadow` and `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.AgentProposalSuperseded`; revalidation, inboxes, `INhAssistantProposalCounts`, feedback and notifications that keep ignoring shadow proposals; a replaced shadow proposal counted once in its own run by `GET admin/agents/{id}/evaluation` and its export; `shadow-superseded` in `AgentProposalStatus` and `ApprovalStatus` of `@newheap/platform-ai-chat` with English and Dutch texts, and `supersededByApprovalId` of `NhAssistantMockProposal`
cases.outcome: SampleEquipmentOrderComposition names the project and item an equipment order changes with ProjectEquipmentProposalGuard, so the intake policy's Supersede keeps one open order per item. While an operator evaluates the intake reviewer in shadow, an administrator starts it on a project to order three laptops: the run records a shadow proposal that never executes. The next run orders five laptops: within the proposal's lifetime the newer shadow order replaces the first, which becomes `shadow-superseded` and names its successor, as a live order would be withdrawn as superseded, and the audit records `AgentProposalSuperseded`. Nothing reaches the order desk and neither order waits in the project approver's inbox. Evaluating the reviewer in shadow therefore shows the newest order, as the live reviewer would. The library tests prove on SQL Server and PostgreSQL that Supersede replaces, Skip reports the newer one as already open and Allow keeps both, that outside the lifetime both are recorded, that the identity rule stays first, that shadow proposals with keys stay out of revalidation and inbox counts, and that the evaluation counts a replaced shadow proposal once, in the run that made it, next to the live proposal a newer one also replaced.

cases.title: A person starts, reads and stops a chat and answers its question from a messaging app
cases.surface: `INhAssistantConversations` (`CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `CancelAsync`) with `NhAssistantNewConversation` (`AgentId`, `Title`) and `NhAssistantConversationOptions` (`Language`, `ActiveDivisionId`); `INhAssistantConversationTurns.AnswerAsync` with `NhAssistantConversationAnswer`; `NhAssistantConversationTurnResult.PendingQuestion`; a new message that closes a question or approval past its lifetime; the Web Push kind `question-waiting` for a question's addressee; `NhAssistantStore.waitExpired` and `submit` over an expired wait in `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`
cases.outcome: The person continues in the messaging app what they would do in the portal. `POST assistant-channel/chats` starts a new chat with the status advisor for the person a link token names, through `INhAssistantConversations.CreateAsync` with the checks of `POST /api/assistant/conversations` (an unknown agent answers `assistant-agent-not-found`), and answers with the link token of the new chat, which expires with the presented link, so starting chats never extends a link. A message there makes the advisor ask which status the launch project gets: the answer carries the question card from `PendingQuestion`, and `POST assistant-channel/chat` reads the linked chat through `GetAsync` with the same card. The person replies with the number of a choice or its text: `SampleAssistantMessagingChannel` maps it to the zero-based choice and answers through `AnswerAsync` in the answer endpoint's order, so a reply that names no choice answers nothing, the advisor continues with the person's choice and the audit records the `messaging-chat` channel on `QuestionAnswered`; the same reply again finds the question answered (`assistant-question-not-pending`). `POST assistant-channel/stops` stops the next waiting question through `CancelAsync`, as the portal's stop button does, and the portal shows it cancelled; someone else's link to the chat finds nothing (`assistant-conversation-not-found`). In the portal the panel sends a message over a question or approval that reads as expired by the browser's clock instead of queueing it, and the server closes the wait first. The library tests prove on SQL Server and PostgreSQL that the services create, read and stop a chat, answer a question and expire it on the application's clock, and refuse another person, another tenant and an agent thread; that a question notifies only its addressee by Web Push while an approval still notifies the person whose turn it is; and that a new message closes a question or approval whose lifetime passed with the late answer's or decision's codes and audit, then starts its turn, while a still valid one keeps the chat busy. The Angular specs prove that the store sends over an expired question or approval, keeps a message queued while the wait is valid, sends a queued message when the wait ends and handles a busy refusal as before, and that the mock API closes an expired question on the next message.

cases.title: The turn of a messaging app names its person, conversation and channel to the situation and the tools
cases.surface: `INhAiTurnPerson` (`User`, `ActorId`, `TenantId`); `NhAiInvocationContext.ConversationId` and `NhAiInvocationContext.Channel` in `INhAssistantTurnContextProvider` and in a governed tool's invocation context
cases.outcome: `SampleAssistantTurnContextProvider` reads the person of the turn from `INhAiTurnPerson` instead of the request, so a turn that the messaging app starts for a person without their request names them in the situation as a turn of the portal does (`User: owner@sample.localhost`, from the claims the channel rebuilt from the user store), and it reads `Channel` to tell the model it answers in the messaging app with a few short sentences of plain text. The project tools' `ProjectAgentCause` reads `ConversationId` and `Channel` from the tool's invocation context, and the status change the person approves from the messaging app publishes `ProjectStatusChangedEvent` with `ChangedInConversationId` and `ChangedThroughChannel`, so the application traces the change to the chat and the channel. The library tests prove on SQL Server and PostgreSQL that a turn context provider, a tool policy and a tool see the conversation, the channel (none for the portal's own turns) and the turn's person in a turn of the endpoints and in a channel's turn, and that nobody is named outside a person's turn.

cases.title: An agent editor's save keeps an MCP server that was assigned while it was open, and the administration assigns servers one by one
cases.surface: `PUT admin/agents/{id}` with `mcpServerIds` omitted, which keeps the agent's assignments, or `[]`, which removes them; `PUT` and `DELETE admin/mcp-servers/{id}/agents/{agentId}` over `INhAssistantMcpServers.AssignAsync` and `UnassignAsync`, answering `NhAssistantMcpServerDto` with the service's codes (`assistant-mcp-server-not-found`, `assistant-agent-not-found`, `mcpServerIds: too-long`) behind the admin policy; the audit kind `AdminMcpServerAssignmentChanged` (`assigned`, `unassigned`); `NhAssistantAdminApiService.assignMcpServer` and `unassignMcpServer`, the optional `AdminAgentInput.mcpServerIds`, and the agent editor (`nh-assistant-admin-agent-editor`), which saves an existing agent without the list and then unassigns and assigns only the servers the administrator changed, with the text `nh-assistant.admin.agent-editor.mcp-servers-failed`
